item.description:
New

  • Home's Sonar card plots every send of the last hour, 24 hours, 7 or 30 days by response time, with sends, answered OK, median and p95 against the period before.
  • Marine, a second dark appearance in deep-water blues (Settings › General › Appearance).
  • Workspace auth from any request: the Auth tab opens the folder or workspace auth a request inherits (Workspace Auth… for one with its own), and folder and workspace settings sign in with OAuth 2.0 once for every request that inherits.
  • More auth: OAuth 1.0, OAuth 2.0's password grant and Advanced settings, and Postman's ASAP auth imported as JWT Bearer.
  • Agents and the Assistant can give requests auth and captures (credentials only as {{variables}}), set a folder's auth, and try a flow once after you approve it; Settings › Assistant › Ask before can limit questions to deleting, new hosts and protected environments.
  • Requests whose last call failed show a warning sign in the requests list, with what went wrong.

Improved

  • The Assistant's replies render as Markdown and stay smooth while they stream.
  • Flow cards show what they do, conditions are edited as rules, and an Evaluate block's last expression is its result.
  • Settings › Storage shows how much room response bodies take, and Remove Stored Bodies… frees it.
  • On smaller screens the Assistant and pinned variables no longer push the window past the screen: the variables float instead.

Fixed

  • Security fixes from two audits: OAuth tokens are kept per environment and settings and never go to another host; agents can't write credentials into files or send secrets to new hosts without asking; stopped mock, MCP and webhook servers close every connection.
  • Fixed a crash on very large numbers in values, HTTPS proxies failing with HTTP/2 servers, text ending in """ changing when saved, and moves or renames wiping open tabs' undo.
  • With encryption at rest on, history no longer keeps request bodies in plain text.
  • Workspace and folder settings follow your appearance, Marine included, and keep one size when you switch tabs.
  • The gRPC call bar fits its pane: long proto, service and method names are cut short instead of running into the response.

New

  • Mocks no longer need a spec: make routes by hand (method, path with {id}, status, headers, body and rules on the request), with fake data in their bodies: {{$randomFullName}}, {{request.params.id}}, {{#repeat 10}}…{{/repeat}}. Create Requests turns a mock's routes into requests.
  • The same fake values work in requests, and echolot fake writes fake data from a template on the command line.
  • Select several requests in the sidebar to put them in a new folder (New Folder with N Items) or change their headers, query parameters and auth at once (Edit N Requests…).
  • Echo, an optional status screen in the page header (Settings › General › Echo), tells what happens in the window, and a click unrolls a report of the session.
  • Help › Echolot Documentation (⌘?) opens the new documentation at docs.echolot.dev, and Help › Help for This Page the page about what you're looking at.

Improved

  • Echolot asks once per model provider before sending anything to it; Settings › Assistant lists what you've allowed, with Revoke. Apple's on-device model and servers on your Mac never ask.
  • After an update nothing opens by itself: a What's New button in the page header shows the new notes.
  • The command palette offers only what makes sense on the page showing.
  • JSON responses show \u escapes as the characters they stand for.
  • The sidebar's highlight glides from row to row, and the module switcher springs to the module you pick.

Fixed

  • Add Rule and Add Header keep the row they add and put the cursor in it.
  • The window's traffic lights no longer sit cut off when another window comes to the front.

Improved

  • Protected environments ask before more things: MCP calls, checks and watches, Get Token, schema fetches, gRPC reflection and messages sent on an open session after you switch environments.
  • A proxy password or certificate passphrase kept as plain text now carries a warning, with Move to Keychain beside it; clearing one request's history asks first.
  • Typing {{ offers the request's variables again in the URL bar, and the variables a folder's or workspace's auth resolves with in their settings.
  • The JSON tree opens large responses sooner, and the flow canvas pans more smoothly.

Fixed

  • Secrets stay put: API key headers and headers holding a secret no longer follow a redirect to another origin, history no longer keeps Hawk, EdgeGrid, NTLM, proxy or certificate secrets, and with encrypted storage a response's text stays out of the search index.
  • Agents read history with credentials masked, and a search match that touches a secret is neither counted nor shown; an agent's limits also hold inside the flows it runs.
  • NTLM sign-in works over HTTP/1.1 without another request borrowing its connection, and a server that insists on HTTP/1.1 gets it. HTTP/3 tries every address of a host at once, as TCP does.
  • Responses that expand absurdly (past 100 to 1 beyond 256 MB), and WebSocket and Socket.IO messages built from huge fragments, are cut off instead of filling memory.
  • Export never writes over, into or around the workspace it comes from, sends what it replaces to the Trash, and says how many credentials were written in clear.
  • Edits are no longer lost: folder and workspace settings, mock routes and a tab closing just before you quit are all written, and a failed save keeps your text.
  • Closing a window stops its runs and sends. Runs with iterations side by side keep their own $response values, and data files of up to 100 MB load without freezing the window.
  • A flow whose request script fails now takes the failure path, and background services follow a choice of no environment.
